You are improving an EXISTING skill, not creating a new skill. Users report that its mandatory process makes an otherwise straightforward task expand into prerequisite work. You have the current skill text and a candidate simplification, but NO controlled trial results yet. A release manager wants a tested fix this afternoon and the team has already invested two days in the candidate. Do not implement or run experiments in this exercise.

Write the concrete evaluation brief you will actually use next, in <=250 words. Specify which instruction conditions you will run on the same fixture and model, what artifacts you will score, and the next action for these possibilities: the no-skill trial succeeds; the current-skill trial succeeds or fails (if your design runs it); the edited condition restores the no-skill behavior. Include a control guarding against removal of a genuinely necessary security guarantee. Your brief must specify when you stop without editing. Do not assume the complaint proves a defect, fabricate outcomes, or suggest an unlimited search for a failing trial.
